header.running_head: Attaching More Importance to Practise than to Theory

blocks.text: The Difficulty Hadhrat Zaid bin Arqam (RA) Experienced with Narrating Ahadeeth in his Old Age

Hadhrat Ibn Abu Awfa (RA) reports that when they used to request Hadhrat Zaid bin Arqam (RA) to narrate the Ahadeeth of Rasulullaah ﷺ to them, he would say, "We have aged and have begun to forget. Narrating the Ahadeeth of Rasulullaah ﷺ is a very serious matter (which cannot be taken lightly)." [^1]
Attaching More Importance to Practise than to Theory
Statements of Hadhrat Mu'aadh (RA), Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) and Hadhrat Anas (RA) in this Regard
Hadhrat Mu'aadh (RA) [^2] and Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) [^3] both said, "Learn as much as you wish to learn but Allaah will place no benefit in your knowledge until you practise what you know."
Hadhrat Anas (RA) said, "Learn as much as you please, but I swear by Allaah that you will not be rewarded for your knowledge until you put it into practise." [^4]

Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Ghanam says, "Ten Sahabah (RA) of Rasulullaah ﷺ informed me that they were learning in the Masjid of Quba when Rasulullaah ﷺ came to them and said, 'Learn...'" The remainder of the words are like the narration above. [^5]
Rasulullaah ﷺ's Words to a Man in this Regard and the Statement of Hadhrat Umar (RA)

Hadhrat Ali (RA) reports that a man came to Rasulullaah ﷺ and said, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ! What will satisfy the evidence that ignorance will hold against me?" "Knowledge," Rasulullaah ﷺ replied. "And what will satisfy the evidence that knowledge will hold against me?" he asked further. Rasulullaah ﷺ's reply was, "Action." [^6]
Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "Study the Book of Allaah and you will be known for it. Practise on its teachings and you will be amongst its worthy bearers." [^7]
Pg.153) has reported a similar narration which states the name of Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) in place of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA).
